message.reasoning_content:
Now let me see the chain tests and data to understand fully — but I can leave that to the worker. I have enough to define acceptance checks: per-unit test commands as given.

Plan: spawn 12 worker instances, one per unit. Each worker gets a task with strict instructions: only modify the assigned unit's implementation file(s), do not modify tests/check.py, run the exact acceptance command from the unit dir, report command + output.

Wait — workers share the workspace (shared default). They'll edit different directories, no conflicts. Good.

Concern: spawning 12 instances may be substantial, but instruction demands one per part. Let's do it. But resource/model: omit model to inherit. Each spawn registers initial task.

Also they should not write REPORT.md (that's mine, integration).

Let me spawn all 12 in parallel calls in one block. Each spawn requires instance_id, instructions, task. Also I want acceptance checks embedded. Also mention: verify with real command; if cannot, say so.

Let me write the instructions generically.

Instance ids: w-csvfix, w-rules, w-ledger, w-schedule, w-intervals, w-flags, w-measure, w-slugify, w-ranges, w-alpha, w-beta, w-chain.

Task text: precise.

For chain, acceptance: cd units/chain && python3 -m pytest -q tests/. Worker needs to read tests and data/orders.csv.

Now spawn. Note spawn creates instance with initial task registered with narrow return path — outcome comes back to me as task result. I need to record task ids. Spawn returns id. I'll then wait on ALL tasks with timer.

Let me do spawns in one block.
